title: Accounts Payable Coordinator
description:
As an Accounts Payable Coordinator in a research-led organisation, based in Oxfordshire, you'll manage supplier invoices, payments, and queries to ensure smooth day-to-day operations. Your role will help keep financial processes accurate and efficient, supporting the wider accounting and finance team.

Client Details

A company in the innovative technology sector located in Oxfordshire.

Description
- Process supplier invoices and ensure timely payments.
- Handle supplier queries and resolve discrepancies efficiently.
- Maintain accurate records of accounts payable transactions.
- Reconcile supplier statements and resolve outstanding issues.
- Support month-end close processes by providing necessary documentation.
- Assist with audits by preparing and organising relevant financial data.
- Ensure compliance with company policies and financial regulations.
- Collaborate with other departments for smooth financial operations.

Profile

A successful Accounts Payable Coordinator should have:
- Experience working with accounting and finance systems.
- Strong attention to detail and organisational skills.
- Ability to handle supplier queries and resolve issues effectively.
- Familiarity with accounts payable processes and reconciliations.
- Knowledge of financial regulations and compliance requirements.
- Good communication and teamwork skills.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from £28,000 to £35,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Competitive benefits package.
- Flexible working options.
- Supportive team culture.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Commercial Property Secretary
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
Macildowie are working with this client based in Oxford to recruit an experienced Legal Secretary to join their Commercial Property team.

Legal Secretary - Commercial Property

Location: Oxford
Salary: £30000
Contract: Permanent
Working Arrangement: Hybrid and Flexible

This is an excellent opportunity to join an established professional services organisation, providing high-quality secretarial and administrative support to a busy team of property specialists.

You'll be working closely with fee earners, helping to ensure commercial property matters progress smoothly and clients receive a professional and responsive service. It's a varied position where organisation, accuracy and the ability to juggle competing priorities will be key.

What will you be doing?

You'll provide comprehensive secretarial and administrative support, including:
- Creating, formatting and amending legal documents and correspondence
- Producing accurate documentation from digital dictation
- Preparing leases, reports and other property-related documents
- Managing diaries, meetings and day-to-day administration for fee earners
- Opening, maintaining and closing client and matter files
- Liaising professionally with clients, agents, solicitors and other external parties
- Supporting commercial property transactions with searches and documentation
- Assisting with Land Registry and Companies House documentation
- Supporting Stamp Duty Land Tax returns, completion paperwork and post-completion administration
- Assisting fee earners with time recording, billing and routine accounting queries
- Scanning, printing and preparing documentation for signature

What are we looking for?

You'll be highly organised, accurate and comfortable working in a fast-paced professional environment.

Previous legal secretarial experience would be highly desirable, with experience supporting Commercial Property or Real Estate teams particularly advantageous.

You'll also need:
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Strong written and verbal communication
- Excellent attention to detail
- Good IT literacy and confidence learning new systems
- Experience working with document and/or case management systems
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines
- A professional and client-focused approach

If you're an experienced Legal Secretary looking for your next opportunity in Oxford, we'd be keen to hear from you.

Please apply with your latest CV for further information.

Macildowie is a specialist recruitment consultancy with a rich history of enhancing the careers of professionals across the Midlands and Northern Home Counties. We have an unrivalled understanding of the local market and are dedicated to helping you achieve your career aspirations.

title: Finance & Office Assistant
description:
Position: Finance & Office Assistant

Location: Oxford (OX44)

Salary: Up to £35,000 per annum

Hours: Monday Friday (full-time)

Experience: Finance Assistant, Accounts Assistant, Sage, Sage Payroll, Office Administration, Credit Control, Purchase Ledger, Sales Ledger, Payroll

The Opportunity

Thompson & Terry Recruitment are delighted to be working with a successful and well-established business, just south of Oxford, who are looking to recruit a Finance & Office Assistant to join their team.

As Finance & Office Assistant, you will support the day-to-day running of the finance and administration functions within a small but busy business. Working closely with colleagues across the business, you will play an important role in supporting payroll, invoicing, supplier administration and general office activities.

The successful Finance & Office Assistant will assist with purchase and sales ledger administration, processing supplier invoices, supporting project costing activities, customer invoicing, credit control, payroll administration, bank reconciliations and record maintenance. In addition to finance responsibilities, the role will include wider office administration duties to support the smooth running of the business.

This opportunity would suit a well-organised candidate who is looking to develop their experience within an SME environment. The successful Finance & Office Assistant will have strong attention to detail, good communication skills and a proactive approach.

The Company

Thompson & Terry Recruitment are proud to be working with a well-established Oxfordshire-based business with a strong reputation within its sector and a track record of delivering specialist projects for a diverse client base.

Operating within a busy and collaborative environment, the business works closely with customers, suppliers and project teams, creating a varied and engaging finance role with broad responsibilities across the organisation.

This position offers the opportunity to gain exposure to a varied finance and administration function while becoming part of a collaborative and supportive team environment.

Requirements
- Minimum 3 years' experience within a finance, accounts or office administration environment
- Relevant finance qualification, with experience using Sage
- Strong communication skills with excellent attention to detail
- Good organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple deadlines
- Experience within an SME environment, with a small business mentality

Thompson & Terry Ltd, trading as Thompson & Terry Recruitment, are an Abingdon-based recruitment agency specialising in placing candidates into roles across Oxfordshire and beyond. We typically recruit for Office Administration Jobs, Sales Jobs, Marketing Jobs, Biotech Jobs, and Executive Search appointments.

No terminology used in this advert is intended to discriminate on the grounds of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. We encourage applications from all suitably qualified individuals.

If you have any accessibility requirements or would like to discuss reasonable adjustments in the recruitment process, please let us know.

PLEASE NOTE: Due to a high volume of applications, if you have not heard from us within 5 working days, unfortunately, your application has been unsuccessful at this time.

title: Procurement Assistant
company: City Site Solutions Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are working with a well-established, family-run main contractor based in Oxfordshire, specialising in high-end residential new-build and refurbishment projects for private clients. Due to continued business growth, they are looking to recruit a Procurement Assistant to join their team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a background in procurement or purchasing who understands that, within high-end residential construction, sourcing the right materials is about more than just price. You will play an important role in sourcing quality products, bespoke finishes and specialist materials that meet the expectations of discerning private clients.

Working closely with the company directors on a daily basis, you will gain valuable insight into the business and its projects, with the opportunity to develop your skills and progress as the company continues to grow.

Key Responsibilities:
- Sourcing and purchasing materials for high-end residential new-build and refurbishment projects.
- Identifying suitable suppliers and obtaining competitive quotations.
- Sourcing bespoke materials, specialist products and high-quality finishes to meet project specifications.
- Liaising with suppliers, subcontractors, site teams and company directors.
- Monitoring orders, deliveries and lead times to ensure materials arrive when required.
- Maintaining strong supplier relationships and identifying opportunities to improve value without compromising quality.
- Supporting the wider team with day-to-day procurement and purchasing activities.

The Ideal Candidate:
- Previous experience in procurement, purchasing or materials sourcing, ideally within construction.
- An understanding of construction materials, finishes and supplier markets.
- An appreciation for quality, attention to detail and the importance of bespoke specifications within high-end residential projects.
- Strong communication, organisation and negotiation skills.
- A proactive approach, with the confidence to liaise directly with company directors and suppliers.
- A desire to learn, develop and build a long-term career within a growing business.

What's on Offer?
- The opportunity to join a respected, family-run construction business.
- Exposure to prestigious, high-end residential projects across Oxfordshire.
- Direct daily contact with company directors and decision-makers.
- Genuine opportunities for career development and progression as the business grows.
- A varied role where quality, craftsmanship and attention to detail are valued.

If you have procurement or purchasing experience and are looking for an opportunity to develop your career within the high-end residential construction sector, we would love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more.

title: Purchase Ledger & Office Administrator
description:
Purchase Ledger & Office Administrator

West Oxfordshire Office Based 26,500 to 28,250

Are you an organised administrator with purchase ledger experience looking for a varied role in a friendly, close knit team?

We're working with an established engineering and manufacturing business in Oxfordshire that is looking for a Purchase Ledger & Office Administrator to support its finance and office operations.

The role:
- Manage the purchase ledger, including invoice processing and supplier reconciliations using Sage 200
- Match purchase orders, delivery notes and invoices
- Process weekly timesheets
- Prepare documents and technical manuals when required
- Order office supplies and coordinate day to day office administration
- Liaise with external suppliers and support multiple departments across the business

What we're looking for:
- Previous Purchase Ledger or Accounts Payable experience
- Experience using Sage or a similar accounts package
- Good Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook
- Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills
- A proactive, energetic and positive approach with the confidence to work independently

What's on offer:
- Salary of 26,500 to 28,250 depending on experience
- Monday to Friday, 8:00am to 4:30pm
- Office based role in West Oxfordshire
- Pension
- On site parking
- 23 days holiday plus bank holidays, increasing with length of service

title: Receptionist/Front of House Co-ordinator
description:
Receptionist/Front of House Co-ordinator

Reporting to: London Office Manager

Office size: Approximately 120 employees

Salary: 30-35k

Role Type: Permanent, Full time, 8:00-5:30

Location: Oxford Street, Full time in the office

Key Responsibilities
- Welcome clients and visitors to the office and promptly notify employees when their guests have arrived.
- Manage the main company telephone lines, directing calls to the relevant person or team and taking and forwarding accurate messages where required.
- Monitor the general enquiries inboxes across the company, ensuring enquiries are promptly forwarded to the appropriate person or team.
- Take ownership of all incoming and outgoing post, including sorting, distributing and arranging couriers and special deliveries.
- Receive parcels and deliveries and ensure they reach the correct recipient.
- Maintain a tidy, welcoming and professional reception and front-of-house area.
- Liaise with the building reception, security, facilities and management teams where required.
- Assist with visitor and employee access, including access cards where applicable.

- Friendly, confident and professional with a welcoming manner.
- An excellent communicator with a strong telephone manner.
- Highly organised with good attention to detail.
- Proactive and comfortable taking ownership of tasks.
- Able to manage calls, emails, visitors and other requests efficiently.
- Confident dealing with clients, employees, suppliers and contractors.
- Comfortable using Microsoft Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 applications.
- Discreet and professional when handling confidential calls, correspondence and visitors.

title: Service Advisor
description:

- Ensure all administrative tasks are completed accurately and on time.

- Handle customer queries and complaints professionally and effectively.

Requirements
- Previous experience as a Service Advisor, Customer Service Advisor, or similar customer-facing role within the automotive industry.
- Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent organisational and administrative abilities.
- Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment.
- Experience using dealership management systems is advantageous.
- Strong attention to detail and customer-focused approach.
- Full UK driving licence preferred.

What's on Offer
- Competitive salary package with realistic OTE of £30,000 - £38,000.
- Manufacturer and in-house training.
- Career development opportunities.
- Pension scheme.
- Employee discounts and benefits package.
- Supportive and professional team environment.
- Modern dealership facilities.

Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will be passionate about customer service, highly organised, and capable of building strong relationships with customers and colleagues alike. You will take pride in delivering an excellent customer experience while helping the aftersales department achieve its performance objectives.

title: Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator
company: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: Advert - Band 3 Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator - Urology We have some exciting opportunities available to join the Urology team as a Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator. We have a variety of posts based at either the Churchill Hospital (Headington). As a Assistant Patient Pathway Administrator, you will work closely with our clinical teams to support the delivery of excellent care to our patients. Your day-to-day role will involve talking with patients and the clinical teams, carrying out a variety of administrative tasks such as booking clinic appointments, scheduling patients into an operating theatre list, and making sure our consultant and nursing teams' clinic letters are processed and sent out to our patients. These roles are ideal for anyone looking to move into the NHS, with good opportunities for career progression both within and outside the department. We welcome applications from recent school leavers or graduates, or those looking for a change, as full training will be given once you start in your role. Informal discussions or visits to the department are welcomed, please do contact either Lisha Collier , Sandeep Thomas or Melanie Bartley for further information. lisha.collier@ouh.nhs.uk sandeep.thomas@ouh.nhs.uk melanie.bartley@ouh.nhs.uk 1. Book new and follow-up outpatient and diagnostic appointments, ensuring that capacity is proactively and efficiently used. This includes booking patients into the correct clinic to ensure that they are seen by the most appropriate clinician. 2. Reschedule outpatient appointments as a result of patients calling the service, in line with local targets and agreed local processes in respect to patient cancellations. 3. Actively review patient DNAs, liaising with the appropriate clinical staff and reschedule patient appointments in line with agreed local processes. 4. Taking telephone calls from patients and actioning their queries or directing them to the appropriate person. 5. Contributing to the management of the daily emails accounts within the department, ensuring that queries are dealt with effectively and efficiently. 6. Completing clinical letters for patients and GPs 7. Adding additional clinic capacity on EPR as directed by management. 8. Liaise with the appropriate teams (e.g. learning disabilities team, translator services etc) to ensure that patients requiring additional support services are not indirectly discriminated. The post holder will be expected to provide day to day administrative support for Urology clinicians within the Urology department. The individual will need to be flexible to meet the competing and evolving demands of the service. There will be an element of cross cover required within the team and an extension of the role to provide administrative support to other services covered by the Urology Team Patient administration underpins the patient journey and supports clinical teams in delivering high quality patient care and can make a real difference to the patient experience. Effective and efficient patient administration supports management through ensuring a high standard of data quality and by making the best use of capacity and resources. The post holder has responsibility for the provision of a professional, comprehensive, and efficient administrative support service for the Urology clinical team

title: Receptionist
company: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
description: To provide a professional and efficient reception service to the Directorate, ensuring that all patients and visitors are welcomed to the department in an appropriate manner whilst adhering to the Trust Policy on Data Quality. To provide a professional, comprehensive and effective administration support service to the administration, nursing and the wider medical teams. To greet patients at reception in a helpful, polite and efficient manner. Deal with enquiries in a sympathetic and professional manner using tact and diplomacy when dealing with anxious patients and relatives. To book follow up appointments accurately ensuring that the correct referral to treatment (RTT) status is recorded in accordance with Trust guidelines. To ensure that all patient demographics are available, up to date and accurate, recording all late bookings, cancellations and DNA's appropriately. To make sure the relevant reception areas within the Directorate are kept tidy and in good repair, with any defects being reported to the relevant line manager. To be able to prioritise your workload and work with minimal supervision. Check all demographics details for patients on arrival, updating these appropriately whilst adhering to the Trust policies for data protection and patient confidentiality. Register patients attendance on EPR inreal-time. To ensure that special requests for additional support in clinics such as interpreters or sign language services are dealt with timeously. To ensure patients are checked in and out of clinic. To carry out reminder phone-calls. To liaise with transport service To undertake further training as and when required. As directed by the patient pathway administrators, assist in any other administrational duties that may be required to ensure full administration service is provided within the Directorate. This may include providing basic cover for the patient pathway administrators during periods of sickness, annual leave or workload increases. Sort and distribute all post received by the department to the appropriate individuals in a prompt and accurate manner. Communicate with patients, carers, clinical and non-clinical staff via the telephone and face to face in a confident and polite manner, whilst maintaining patient confidentiality. Conversations can be of a sensitive and complex nature.
